decision.summary: 30 of 33 findings are evidence-backed; 3 were insufficient and recorded for follow-up.

findings.statement: NVIDIA is evaluating opportunities to expand its AI infrastructure business in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
The internal strategy brief identifies infrastructure constraints involving power, cooling, connectivity, and data residency.
Opportunity A – Saudi Cloud AI Cluster estimated value $42 million.
Primary blocker for Opportunity A is power capacity and data center delivery schedule.
Opportunity B – UAE Enterprise AI Platform estimated value $18 million.
Primary blockers for Opportunity B are data residency, security review, and procurement approval.
Saudi Arabia may offer opportunities associated with large‑scale data center projects and enterprise AI adoption.
Saudi Arabia could provide larger project‑scale opportunities.
UAE could offer selected opportunities with shorter enterprise deployment paths.
Intel offers the Gaudi® 3 AI Accelerator as the HL-325L OAM mezzanine card, a high‑density form factor designed for massive AI workloads in data‑center deployments.
Intel also supplies the Gaudi® 3 AI Accelerator on the HLB-325 baseboard, a dedicated carrier board that supports the accelerator in rack‑mount configurations.

Intel’s Xeon Scalable platform, documented in the Xeon® Scalable Platform product brief, delivers AI acceleration across its processor line, supporting up to 40 cores per socket for high‑throughput inference and training workloads.

Target customers and positioning: compared with NVIDIA, Intel is comparable. Intel positions its Gaudi 3 accelerator and Xeon Scalable platform for cloud service providers and enterprises building AI infrastructure, matching NVIDIA’s target segment.
In October 2024, the Public Investment Fund (PIF) of Saudi Arabia and Google Cloud partnered to build a global artificial intelligence hub near Dammam.
The deep learning segment accounted for the largest market revenue share in 2025.
In January 2024, Informatica unveiled Saudi Arabia’s first AI-oriented intelligent data management cloud platform and set up a new Point of Delivery (PoD) in Riyadh.
60.8% of survey respondents in the UAE and Saudi Arabia say they would definitely upgrade to an AI PC.
The National Strategy for Data and Artificial Intelligence (NSDAI) targets an investment of USD 20 billion in AI technologies.
Only 6% of consumers currently own an AI PC.
In October 2024, the Public Investment Fund (PIF) of Saudi Arabia and Google Cloud partnered to build a global artificial intelligence hub near Dammam.
The deep learning segment accounted for the largest market revenue share in 2025.
The operations segment accounted for the largest market revenue share in 2025.
The UAE data center market is expected to grow at an average rate of 3.43% between 2022 and 2027.
Up to $1 billion in additional investments are projected by 2026.
The cybersecurity market in the UAE is expected to grow to a value of $4.51 billion by 2025.
Saudi Arabia's Edge AI Hardware Market was valued at USD 11,465 million in 2025.
The market is projected to reach USD 22,999 million by 2030.
The market is growing at a compound annual growth rate of 14.9% from 2025 to 2030.
A reported deal to allow the UAE to import 500,000 NVIDIA AI chips annually starting in 2025 shows a concrete procurement signal for the region.
NVIDIA posts generate high engagement on X (average 1,241.93 interactions per item) and attract strong positive reactions to programs such as the Open Agent Safety Platform and the Inception program.
NVIDIA accounts for 64.5% of mentions in the collected set, while Intel accounts for 24.0%, indicating a visibility gap for Intel among regional AI computing discussions.
